Claire — great to hear you're ready to proceed. Attached is a concise POC packet (Redwood_POC_Scope_v1.pdf) plus a draft 3-week timeline (poc-timeline.xlsx). Below is the quick recap and implementation checklist you asked for.

POC objective (3 weeks):
- Validate Redwood inference for clinical note summarization at production-like latency and throughput; preserve PHI handling choices and ensure output quality meets stakeholder thresholds.

Success criteria (PASS if all met):
1) Accuracy: mean ROUGE-L improvement of summary quality compared to current baseline (internal metric) — target: >= +12% on our sampled set.
2) Latency: 95th percentile generation < 650ms for 512-token context on dedicated instance configuration.
3) Throughput: sustained 60 requests/min with 200 concurrent users using burst capacity; no more than 2% error rate.
4) Cost-per-1K-tokens: within 15% of the projected estimate in the attached cost worksheet.
5) Security/compliance: data retention and KMS integration validated (SOC2-ready evidence shared).

Proposed timeline & milestones (high level):
Week 0 (this week): kickoff, dataset handoff (sample set), credentials & networking (VPC peering if needed).
Week 1: integration & baseline runs (SDK + API smoke tests), initial tuning.
Week 2: load tests (throughput/latency), quality tuning, prompts/temperature optimization.
Week 3: final evaluation, handoff, acceptance sign-off, and next steps for production.

Ownership (Redwood / Clearview):
- POC lead (Redwood): Hannah Schmitt — commercial lead, weekly syncs and acceptance coordination.
- Technical lead (Redwood): Ben Carter — SDK/API integration, streaming setup, perf tuning.
- Legal/procurement (Redwood): Marissa Cole — contract & SOW coordination.
- POC lead (Clearview): Claire James — business acceptance & stakeholder coordination.
- Technical lead (Clearview): Tom Ruiz — data access, infra, and test schedule.

Implementation checklist (high priority items):
- API keys & temp credentials (Redwood creates a scoped key for trial)
- Network: confirm egress policy or VPC peering (if required)
- Sample dataset: Clearview to share 200 clinical notes (de-identified) by EOD Fri
- SDK selection: we recommend using Redwood Python SDK with streaming enabled for the summarization endpoint (see Ben's notes below)
- Acceptance test set: 50 holdout notes for final pass/fail run
- Observability: trace & token usage dashboard access granted to Clearview (read-only)

Attachments included: Redwood_POC_Scope_v1.pdf, poc-timeline.xlsx, sdk-integration-snippets.txt

Next steps (for this Friday EOD):
1) Claire/Tom — confirm owners and share the sample dataset.
2) Marissa — send draft SOW for procurement to Claire.
3) Ben & Tom — quick tech sync (30m) to validate SDK requirements and VPC needs; propose time slots.

If that looks good I'll schedule the kickoff.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Lead — Redwood Inference

Claire / Tom / Hannah — quick technical follow-up with concrete integration steps and minimal examples so your engineers can hit the ground running. I attached a short snippets file but included the most important bits inline here too.

Recommended integration surface:
- Endpoint: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate/summarize
- Payload (non-streaming): {
  "model": "redwood-rlhf-2k",
  "input": "<clinical_note_text>",
  "max_tokens": 256,
  "temperature": 0.0,
  "response_format": "json_summary"
}
- Streaming: use the /v1/stream/generate route to get tokens as they are produced; useful to show progressive summary in the UI and reduce perceived latency.

Python SDK snippet (streaming):

from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED_KEY")
with client.stream("summarize", model="redwood-rlhf-2k", input=note_text, max_tokens=256, temperature=0.0) as stream:
    for chunk in stream:
        # chunk.partials contain token text; update UI progressively
        print(chunk.text, end="")

Key engineering notes:
- KV cache: If you do multi-turn summarization (context across multiple notes), enable per-session KV caching to avoid reprocessing repeated context. For single-note summarization it's optional.
- Token limits: max context 4096 tokens; we recommend trimming clinical templates before passing to reduce noise.
- Batching: Redwood runtime supports continuous batching; if you expect bursts, configure the SDK client to batch up to 8 requests with a 50ms aggregation window for improved throughput.
- Tool calling: If you want structured extraction (diagnoses / meds) alongside the summary, use the function-calling extension. We can provide a schema and examples — Ben can run a short mapping exercise with Tom during the sync.
- Observability: include header X-Trace-Id to correlate logs with the console dashboard.

Network & security:
- If Clearview prefers VPC peering we can provision a Private Deployment trial. Otherwise the hosted API is fine with strict IP allow-lists.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys; proof artifacts for SOC2 are in the attached POC packet.

Proposed quick tech sync slots (30 min):
- Fri 23 Apr 2027 11:00-11:30 PT
- Mon 26 Apr 2027 09:00-09:30 PT

I'll join the call and walk through the SDK snippet and streaming behavior.

-ben
